record.text: We onboard roughly four new EU clients a year, and every single one requires us to sign their own data processing agreement under GDPR; our lead developer is spending almost two weeks per contract just reviewing clauses, which is pulling him off billable work and we can't afford an in-house lawyer.
record.detail: Every new EU client we sign requires us to agree to their own data processing agreement before we can start work. The language in these contracts varies significantly — some are straightforward, some include clauses around sub-processor lists, audit rights, and data residency that need careful reading before we sign. Right now our lead developer, Marko Ilić, is the person who reviews all of them because he has the most experience with how our systems actually handle data. He estimates he spends close to two weeks of billable time per contract on this review, which at our project margins is genuinely painful. We have tried using a standard template from a Serbian IT industry association as a reference point, but clients do not accept our version — they want us to sign theirs. We cannot justify a full-time in-house lawyer for four contracts a year. We are looking for a practical way to speed up this review process and reduce the burden on our technical staff, whether that is a structured checklist, a clause-comparison tool, or a repeatable workflow that someone without a legal background can actually follow.
